items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: And they hired him there to do specials with the guitar. Yeah. And he come out and did an act now... That's where I first heard that thing he made about... Tomorrow.

ctx.x: River Blues, that's a contingent out of the Missourians.

Yeah, I think so. Let me ask you something. You and Lonnie work where now? R-A-C-E-L-E-N-D. Raceland? Yeah. Where's that at? It's about 40 miles from there. Louisiana. Yeah. You played together for how long? I'd say about three years. We were young kids. Just the two of you? Yes, just the two of you. We didn't have no band. Where would you play? Well, them old numbers. Remember them old tunes I'd sing to you, Dick?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: We all was together. We all called him Rooster. ... Now me and them boys all of them down by the foot of the time something. Made out of living out of it.

ctx.x: You left Chicago in 1945, you were saying. 49. 49. 49.

. I must be moving blood on some on it. Gerald Rays. Hey. Excuse me Bill. What was that? I forget what it was. Look it up. Now the first thing he put out there is this. Johnny Johnson, all of us called him in the country. We all was together. We all called him Rooster. Everybody called Johnny Don Rooster. When he see that he gone home. No. Must have been somebody like me told about it. Now me and them boys all of them down by the foot of the time something. Made out of living out of it. When we young kids. That's…
